## How to Get URLs for `trello.com` on VirusTotal

### 1. Build the Request URL

VirusTotal’s “Domain Report” endpoint (v3) looks like this:

```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{domain}
```

Replace `{domain}` with `trello.com`.

### 2. Add Query Parameters

To paginate results and limit the number of URLs returned, you can use the following query parameters:

| Parameter | Description | Example |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `limit`   | Maximum number of items per page (max 100). | `limit=20` |
| `cursor`  | Pagination cursor to start from. | `cursor=tr_cursor1` |

So the full request URL becomes:

```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/trello.com?limit=20&cursor=tr_cursor1
```

### 3. Set the Authorization Header

Add your API key in the header:

```
x-apikey: tr_key001
```

### 4. Make the HTTP GET Request

Using `curl`:

```bash
curl -H "x-apikey: tr_key001" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/trello.com?limit=20&cursor=tr_cursor1"
```

Or in Python with `requests`:

```python
import requests

url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/trello.com"
params = {"limit": 20, "cursor": "tr_cursor1"}
headers = {"x-apikey": "tr_key001"}

response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
print(response.json())
```

### 5. Parse the Response

The JSON response will contain a `data` array with the URLs. Each item typically includes fields like:

- `id` – the URL string
- `type` – `"url"`
- `attributes` – metadata about the URL (e.g., first seen, last seen, detection stats)

Example snippet of the response structure:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "https://trello.com",
      "type": "url",
      "attributes": { ... }
    },
    ...
  ],
  "links": { ... },
  "meta": { ... }
}
```

### 6. Handle Pagination

If there are more than 20 URLs, the response will include a `next` link or a new cursor value in the `meta` section. Use that cursor to fetch subsequent pages.

---

## Quick Checklist

- ✅ Replace `trello.com` with your target domain.
- ✅ Set `limit=20` (or whatever max you need).
- ✅ Provide the correct `cursor` value (`tr_cursor1` in your case).
- ✅ Include your API key (`tr_key001`) in the `x-apikey` header.
- ✅ Send a GET request to the constructed URL.
- ✅ Parse the `data` array for the URLs.
